Albers répond par télégramme à Barr et d: Albers responds by telegram to Barr and defines its three terms: structure (inherent character of raw material: wood grain, yarn fiber, marble crystal), invoice (aspect dominated by material work: hammered metal, twisted yarn, combed hair), texture (similar elements combined in a constructive organ: weaving, braiding, knitting, masonry) Telegram; Examples: wood grain, yarn fiber, marble crystal, hammered metal, twisted wire, combed hair, weaving, braiding, knitting, masonry
Le Brooklyn Daily Eagle publie un articl: The Brooklyn Daily Eagle publishes an article about an art teacher fleeing the Nazis who came to teach — press testimony about the emigration of the Albers. title translated: “Professeur d'art, fuyant les nazis, ici pour enseigner”
Discours d'Albers à un déjeuner de colle: Speech from Albers at a college fund-raising luncheon at New York.
Une partie de la faculté tente d'évincer: Part of the faculty tries to eject Rice and threatens to break the college if it does not leave; motive: insult and distance donors and students; real motive according to her: her disciples would feel betrayed since the previous year and seek security in success; personal rivalries in addition; Rice was the college, which no longer holds people together; Allan Sly will not return next year, seeking security and fame, which hit the college hard because music was the most important thing of the year; She is waiting for a new teacher because Sly has become an inhibiting force for her: her unattainable standards paralyze her at the expected “dans les six semaines” explosion piano Consequences: departure of Sly announced, decline of the prestige of Rice, speculation on another foundation by her faithful
Quelques mois avant la guerre, les Fleis: A few months before the war, the Fleischmanns left Nazi Germany on the same boat, Orinoco, only two years earlier. Toni notes in his diary the pain of permanent exile and the moments of happiness found (arrival in Mexico City, tropical landscape). Toni Journal: “¿ahora qué?”; Orinoco boat Consequences: Parents move to Mexico
Les Fleischmann débarquent de l'Orinoco,: Fleischmann landed from Orinoco, the same boat as two years earlier for a vacation; Josef and Anni welcome them to the port Words : Toni : “Aujourd'hui, il y a deux ans que nous embarquions pour ce même voyage sur ce même bateau… Aujourd'hui nous quittons notre pays natal, que nous devons quitter pour toujours” Atmosphere : Double : joy of reunion, sorrow of exile Issue : The heartbreaking emigration of the German family under Nazism
Les parents d'Anni débarquent de l'Orino: Anni's parents landed from Orinoco, the same boat as their 1937 voyage; Josef and Anni are waiting for them at the dock; Toni notes in his diary the contrast between the two trips. Words : Toni : “il y a exactement deux ans, le même bateau, l'Orinoco… c'était un voyage pour revoir nos enfants ; aujourd'hui c'est un départ de notre patrie, que nous devons quitter pour toujours” Atmosphere : Joy mixed with despair of emigrants ; Tropical Campaign Lived Like “un magnifique, rare cadeau” Issue: Final Exile of a Jewish German Family
Discours d'Albers à la première assemblé: Speech by Albers at the first general meeting of the 7th year of the college
Discours d'ouverture d'Albers au début d: Opening speech of Albers at the beginning of the 7th year of the college.
Scott, instructeur à Harvard, écrit enth: Scott, instructor at Harvard, writes enthusiastically to Albers after a design workshop.
Albers prononce le discours « On Educati: Albers delivers the speech “On Education and Art Education”, tapuscrit kept in the archives of the Josef and Anni Albers Foundation. Tapuscrit, JAAF Archive
Albers lit un texte non titré au meeting: Albers reads an untitled text at the Black Mountain College meeting held at the Museum of Modern Art. Text retained at JAAF Archives.
Allocution d'Albers lors d'une réunion d: Speech by Albers at an Black Mountain College meeting at the Museum of Modern Art. Text kept at the Albers Foundation, 3 pages.
Réunion de levée de fonds : Gropius raco: Fundraising meeting: Gropius tells about his stay at Black Mountain, the spirit of cooperation in meeting with students; it presents with Breuer the model of glass houses on stilts; Albers, a star visitor, delivers his profession of educational faith; photographers of the Herald Tribune believe the two architects around the model. Words: Gropius: “letting the life form the house”; Albers: “One can suffocate from knowledge, never from experience” Atmosphere: New York Elegance, Descriptive Idealism, Model Under Projectors Issue: The Mountain College Sold to America
Article du New York Herald Tribune montr: New York Herald Tribune article showing Breuer and Gropius with a mock-up of a new building planned for Lake Eden campus. article of 10 January 1940 with model Consequences: construction project not carried out as is; the Studies Building will be built around 1940-41
« Tradition and Technique Are Watchwords: “Tradition and Technique Are Watchwords at Yale's School of the Fine Arts”: opening photo showing advanced sculpture students drawing a bare model; realistic nude paintings; students learning supervision and gilding; one crushes its colors with mortar; A fourth-year student dresses a model to study the effect of a drape on his knees. Life, 12 February 1940, pp. 44-47.
Lors de la fête de la Saint-Valentin, le: At Valentine's Day, the costumes of students are strikingly similar to the study of subjects done in class earlier in the day; Albers documents them in color slides. Community life and educational activities merge, as at Bauhaus.
En février 1940, Rice ayant prolongé son: In February 1940, when Rice extended his leave without resigning, Wunsch wrote the letter concluding the struggle: his resignation would be appreciated; Rice had promised to send it if it was necessary to avoid the closure of the college; half of the faculty refuses to face another internal struggle in addition to economic insecurity; everything is a loss of confidence in his ability to work in a small community. At Nell, separately: Rice is responsible for this loss of confidence; “Dieu sait que nous ne voulions pas la perdre”; Without him, we will feel less depressed and more autonomous. Letters of February 16, 1940. Consequences: Resignation of Rice.
Wunsch écrit à Rice pour réclamer la dém: Wunsch writes to Rice to claim the promised resignation, invoking half the exhausted faculty and loss of confidence; to Nell, a separate letter explains that Rice alone is responsible. Words: “Tout se résume à ceci : nous avons perdu confiance en votre capacité à travailler dans une petite communauté comme celle-ci.”; Nell : “Dieu sait que nous ne voulions pas perdre confiance en lui.” Atmosphere : sad firmness Issue : The permanent expulsion of the founder
Albers déclare qu'à Black Mountain l'ens: Albers declares that at Black Mountain the teaching of art is “au centre de toute activité”, internal challenge point Consequences: The Future Schism Art vs. Arts and Science
John Dewey écrit une lettre à Theodore D: John Dewey writes a letter to Theodore Dreier, quoted in the main text
Atelier de cinq jours intitulé « Fundame: Five-day workshop entitled “Fundamental Design of Today”, transcribed; Albers repeats Rembrandt's anecdote already published in 1934; he had also treated drawing in an unpublished text “Drawing” in the same year. Preserved full transcript (JA Papers). Consequences: Dissemination of his BMC pedagogy outside the college.
Albers présente un texte sans titre à la: Albers presents an untitled text at the first general meeting of the College. Manuscript preserved, BMCR.
Discours sans titre prononcé à la premiè: Speech without title delivered at the first general assembly of the college, tapuscrit preserved.
Marcia Winn écrit « Hardware Art Nicks E: Marcia Winn writes “Hardware Art Nicks Edge of Priority Knife”: In the context of the war restrictions, the materials of Anni Albers' weaving metal compete with military priorities. Chicago Daily Tribune, November 15, 1941
Titre de journal du 4 avril 1942 : « CLA: Journal title of 4 April 1942: “CLARENCE DAWSON BURIED HERE MON. Husband of Cara Byars Dawson Succumbs After Long Illness” ; In front of the coffin, the child stares, the eyes dry, the father's face — waxy skull, bluffed, ugly — then diverts the head: “Ce n'est pas mon père”; cool and rainy day; While the procession crosses the city towards the cemetery, it looks through the window at the April trees, lawns, houses, cars; the air is fresh and moist as the earth where it descends; at home, in the Victorian living room with curtains drawn, her mother sitting in a capitinated armchair drinks a glass of sherry; aunts fix the ground; One of them said the first: you'll have to be a good boy. Sherry, upholstered chair, curtains drawn
L'enfant fixe le visage cireux du mort e: The child fixes the waxy face of the dead and turns the head away; cool and rainy day; procession through the city, April trees seen from the window; In the Victorian lounge with curtains drawn, the mother drinks a sherry, aunts fix the floor; An aunt tells her you'll have to be a good boy. Words: “That's not my father”; “il faudra être un bon garçon” Atmosphere: Fresh and humid air, Victorian silence, sherry Issue: Repressed mourning, dry eyes
Le collège écrit au National Selective S: The College writes to the National Selective Service Board to save at least its oldest teachers from conscription; Major T. Upton replied on 14 May that each case would be decided individually by the local offices.
Fortune envoie un télégramme d'enquête ;: Fortune sends an investigation telegram; BMC responds on an undated typed page — a good profile of the effects of war on the college.
Un télégramme daté du 16 décembre 1942 e: A telegram dated December 16, 1942 was decided by the meeting of the Board of Fellows of the same day.
Dans une conférence, Albers discute l'ar: In a lecture, Albers discusses the artificiality of the single point-of-view perspective integrated with camera lenses and describes photographs as the flattest image type
Dreier remercie Forbes d'un don de trois: Dreier thanks Forbes for a gift of three thousand dollars and its past help. $3,000
Une conférence, prévue à BMC, est finale: A conference, scheduled at BMC, was eventually moved to Talladega College for reasons that Duberman could not elucidate.
Dreier correspond avec Marshall Field (2: Dreier corresponds to Marshall Field (24 March 1942, 24 July 1943), which offers $10,000; other solicitations from the Babbotts of John Burchard. Sum: $10,000
Invité par Albers en 1943, Charlot note: Invited by Albers in 1943, Charlot notes in his diary: September 6, arrival at the Albers, “fotos admirables de México”; the 7, his lecture on Mexico, reception at the Albers with wine; He was asked to teach the following summer. Albers also organizes an Charlot exhibition at BMC the same year. Charlot Journal, 1943; wine served at reception Consequences: Return of Charlot with family the following summer
Invité par Albers, Charlot visite le col: Invited by Albers, Charlot visits the college: September 6 at the Albers (photos of Mexico admired); the evening 7th, conference on Mexico, reception at the Albers with wine; He was offered to teach the next summer. Charlot Journal: “Sept. 6. To Albers... Evening: My talk on Mexico. The reception at Albers. Wine. I am asked to teach next summer.” Consequences: Exhibition of Charlot's work at the college later in the year; return the following summer
Le 6, Charlot arrive chez les Albers et: The 6, Charlot arrives at the Albers and admires his photographs of Mexico; On the evening of the 7th, he gave his lecture on Mexico, followed by a reception at the Albers with wine; We propose him to teach the following summer Words: Charlot Journal: “Fotos admirables de México tomadas por él”, “Mi charla sobre México. La recepción en Albers. Vino. Me piden que dé clases el verano que viene” Atmosphere: Warm, friendly, around wine Issue: Seal the invitation of Charlot to teach at BMC
Le 6, Charlot se rend chez les Albers et: The 6, Charlot goes to the Albers and admires his photos of Mexico; On the evening of the 7th, he gave his lecture on Mexico, followed by a reception at the Albers with wine; He was offered to teach the next summer. Words : Charlot Journal : “Evening: My talk on Mexico. The reception at Albers. Wine. I am asked to teach next summer.” Atmosphere : Friendly, warm, around the wine and images of Mexico Issue : Mexico enters college by the person of Charlot ; The birth of friendship and collaboration (fresques de 1944)
Mariage deux jours et deux ans après Pea: Marriage two days and two years after Pearl Harbor. Witness: Brother Peter, Father Bart Vanderschellen (Dutchman who fought in the Spanish War), and Alain the New Yorker cartoonist (Daniel Brustlein). Then a drink in a bar in the centre, without any fat, then back to the workshop where everyone takes back the work. Marie Fried, the mother, refuses to attend. Elaine claims that Gruen was twenty-three years old; it had twenty-five consequences: union of which all foresee tensions
Un matin de décembre : robe bleu marine: December morning: navy blue dress already worn, sister's bag, $9.50 wedding ring, no mother or Conrad; then either a bar or a cafeteria lunch offered by Biala and Brustlein; immediate return to work at the workshop Words: Elaine will note that the day is Emily Dickinson's birthday and falls “deux ans et deux jours” after Pearl Harbor Atmosphere: summary, without fascist, almost a festive non-event Issue: the union of two painters who resume work in the afternoon itself
Le recteur entre dans le lobby où les ét: The Rector enters the lobby where students celebrate New Year's Eve; too much wine, according to him, turned the “petits garçons et filles” into Greenwich Villagers enlaced; He immediately left, deeply upset, and told John Evarts Words: Wunsch: “too much wine had changed the little boys and girls into Greenwich Villagers”; “I didn't stay very long” Atmosphere: Student holiday seen by a stern and pudibund eye Issue: Conflict between order and sensuality in the heart of the war community
Première lecture en anglais de la pièce: First reading in English of the play (not named here) given to the college.
Gropius écrit à Dreier ; lettre conservé: Gropius writes to Dreier; Letter kept at the Bauhaus Archives in Berlin, a sign of their correspondence followed during the war. Letter of 16 April 1944, Bauhaus Archive, Berlin Consequences: Maintenance of the relationship that will lead Dreier to include Gropius in the sending of his resignation
En réunion de faculté, Straus déclare qu: At the faculty meeting, Straus states that there are certain things to be faced about Black: Black is “étrange”, the “nous sommes tous des êtres humains” formula is too small and too simple; it does not mean that we are superior but that there are defined differences; He doubted it was the college's role to change these things. Typed notes of the meeting Consequences: Some call him racist (anonymously)
Albers écrit à René d'Harnoncourt (MoMA): Albers writes to René d'Harnoncourt (MoMA): to eliminate friction and percussion, it would be good, if not necessary, to also admit students of the red and yellow races — Indians, Chinese, Japanese American; Thus the action would not appear to oppose racial prejudice and would lose its character of aggression. Consequences: Reveals the fear of going too far too fast
Dans une lettre à John Evarts du 8 juill: In a letter to John Evarts dated July 8, 1944, Wunsch describes the first day of the Kolisch workshop as an “privilege”: disagreements over the interpretation of a sentence, discussions, explanations, hard and concentrated work; for him, a dramatic adventure to see the order born from work.
Série de réunions ordinaires et spéciale: Series of ordinary and special meetings of the faculty at the heart of the crisis; Lowinsky remember their indignation shared with Anni Albers in front of Graaff Frances “irresponsabilité”. Minutes at the Raleigh Archives; interview with the Lowinsky of April 10, 1967. Consequences: Escalade towards the August 1944 sanctions and departures.
Une note datée du 19 juillet 1944 est dé: A note dated 19 July 1944 is deposited at the Raleigh Archives; Gregory remembers (interview of June 18, 1967).
Selon un récit non citable, le Board aur: According to an uncitable account, the Board would have calculated that Frances would not leave if Bentley left, but that Bentley would leave if Frances left — hence a fire directed at it. Anni Albers, according to two anonymous witnesses, counted the voices behind the scenes (“celui qui a compté les nezs et calculé que cela marcherait, c'est Anni”) and played the compromises again; she “ne parlait jamais beaucoup en public”. Special meetings of the Board of August 1, 6 and 8, 1944. Consequences: Departures of Bentley and Graaff.
Jalowetz écrit au Board of Fellows le 14: Jalowetz wrote to the Board of Fellows on August 14, 1944; Wunsch confirms that his sympathies went to the starters. Bentley describes him as someone “qui ne peut pas vivre avec l'hostilité”. Also a four-page, undated, typed Jalowetz report.
Martin arrive directement de la gare au: Martin arrives directly from the station when Bodky plays the first twelve runaways of the well temperate Second Keyboard. It comes from the station on foot to the place of performance
Document de cinq pages résumant les disc: Five-page document summarizing the discussions on the work programme at the community meeting on Tuesday, 13 November 1945. Consequences: Followed by “Recommendations of Community Meeting” of 27 November 1945; opening of a Faculty Study Group on “les buts de l'éducation à BMC”, a second meeting of which was never scheduled
Wallen décrit son schéma (« three-step p: Wallen describes its scheme (“three-step process”) in a letter to its parents: first identify symptoms, then examine the underlying causes, and finally formulate prescriptions to deal with the problem. Letter of 25 March 1946; also a one-page notice distributed before the meeting
Gropius écrit à Albers pour le remercier: Gropius writes to Albers for thanking him for guiding his daughter, helping her “à combiner son talent de pensée abstraite avec son talent visuel”. Letter to the Western Regional Archives, Asheville.
Article “It's Art, Baby” of Robert C. Rouark in the Philadelphia Evening Bulletin (27 September 1946); preceded in May 1946 by an article “Black Mountain College” in Junior Bazaar (p. 130-133 et seq.). Consequences: Mediating the college in the mainstream press
Dernière lettre citée à Perdekamp ; entr: Last letter quoted in Perdekamp; BBC interviews (21 June 1968), Finkelstein (2 January and 2 November 1966), Duberman (11 November 1967) as sources of the book.
La nomination de Sawyer est entérinée da: La appointment of Sawyer was endorsed in the minutes of the Yale Council of 19 April 1947, under the chairmanship of Charles Seymour. Consequences: He recruited Albers in 1950
Lettre de trois pages de Levi ; Albers é: Three-page letter from Levi; Albers writes in pencil at the top of the first page: “Consider [this] partly an answer of the board [of fellows]”. Three pages; pencil annotation; JAAF archive
Albers reçoit les trois pages de Levi, p: Albers receives the three pages of Levi, takes a pencil and writes at the top of the first page that it is partly a response from the Fellows' Council Words: Annotation: “Consider [this] partly an answer of the board [of fellows]” Atmosphere: Administrative Coldness Issue: The Levi-Albers conflict fits into the documents
Albers écrit à Ted et Bobbie Dreier ; le: Albers writes to Ted and Bobbie Dreier; Dreier responses are lost or destroyed. La financial situation of the college is complex. La family Dreier holds a second-tier mortgage of $16,500 on the property of Black Mountain Consequences: Background to Rectorate Taking by Albers
Dans une lettre au Board of Fellows, Alb: In a letter to the Board of Fellows, Albers requests to be paid “au moins 1000 dollars” for its second semester work. 1000 dollars minimum, second half
Goodman signe à New York une suite de pr: Goodman signs to New York a suite of ironic precepts addressed to who would plan to create a Universe. dated and signed “New York City June 1, 1947”
Dans une lettre confidentielle à Ise Gro: In a confidential letter to Ise Gropius, Dreier evokes the possibility of settling in post-war Germany, while still hoping that things will work out for Black Mountain. Letter of August 22, 1947, Bauhaus Archive, Berlin Consequences: Shows the discouragement of Dreier one year before his resignation
Traîneau acheté pour Johnny au cas où ;: Sled bought for Johnny in case; miraculously white world in the morning; descents from the road, students staying on campus take turns under Johnny in the descent and climb him up; gentle slope of the garden. Rare luges; sledge attached to a laundry basket with the two children, overturned in a ditch, cut under the eye of Frances, treated at the infirmary by a nurse student with a curly brown beard that she caressed without crying.
Au moment de prendre la route, Cage et C: When you get on the road, Cage and Cunningham discover under their car a lot of presents — paintings, drawings and all sorts of things — a sign of appreciation and affection. Atmosphere: Discreet emotion, mutual gratitude. Issue: Seal the invitation to return for the summer of 1948.
Le comité se réunit les 24-25 avril 1948: The Committee met on 24-25 April 1948; four members report on architecture, four on painting and sculpture (Albers, Elliott, Kratina, Osborn). The report by President Leslie Cheek Jr. recommends a basic curriculum for all new students; The voice of Albers is recognizable: no formula to copy, develop its own procedures by direct experience, “think in situations, not by predigested theory”. An annex includes “Collaborative Problems” in teams on a visual problem of the industrial era.
Lettre manuscrite adressée à la faculté: Handwritten letter addressed to the faculty of the college evaluating the oral and written work of Nakata for the graduation exam; signed among others “Regis”. Reproduced in facsimile. Header “Black Mountain College”, dated June 7, 1948. Consequences: Graduation of Nakata.
À la réunion spéciale de la faculté du 1: At the special meeting of the faculty on July 12, 1948, Goldowski expressed its annoyance that he could not learn “de divers membres de la faculté quelles idées pouvaient être considérées comme représentatives des principes du collège”. Consequences: Sign of the ideological confusion of the crisis
Lettre de M.C. aux Dreier du 25 juillet: Letter from M.C. to the Dreier of 25 July 1948 (including a more complete draft given to Duberman); She described policy disagreement “expansion contre pauvreté”, which was then developed by Stephen Forbes in an interview (1-2 April 1967). partially unpublished draft Consequences: Key Document of the 1948 Crisis
Richards demande franchement aux Dreier: Richards frankly asks the Dreier if it is wrong: do they intend to make BMC a smooth jewel of modern design — which costs money — when it prefers disorder, more teachers and fewer students? Words: “Dites-moi si je me trompe… je préférerais un campus débraillé, plus de professeurs, moins d'étudiants, et moins d'argent.” Atmosphere: friendly frankness, deep disagreement Issue: leadership of the college at stake, one year before split
Richards traduit la pièce de Satie (1913: Richards translates Satie's piece (1913) for its first production in English; It is played with Fuller and Elaine by Kooning, directed by two students of Richards, Helen Livingston and Arthur Penn. Consequences: Penn to become Hollywood director (The Miracle Worker, 1962; Bonnie and Clyde, 1967)
Aux réunions de faculté des 27 et 28 aoû: At faculty meetings on August 27 and 28, 1948, Albers expressed hope for external financial assistance (a promise of $2,000 already received) and planning another art institute for the following summer with “un grand nombre d'étudiants”. $2,000 promise Consequences: Materialize Summer Institute 1949
Dreier envoie sa démission de Black Moun: Dreier sends his resignation from Black Mountain College and includes Gropius on the mailing list, a sign of their intimacy — the correspondence of the Bauhaus Archive tells of Dreier's disillusionment and departure from the radical institution he had largely contributed to creating. Consequences: End of the most difficult post-war college period; starting a founding pillar
Dreier écrit aux Gropius que « le dé est: Dreier writes to the Gropius that “le dé est jeté”: he cannot resolve to undertake a new reorganization of the college and announces that he wants to leave. He includes the Gropius in sending his resignation letter, testimony of their proximity. A few days of reflection before the letter of August 31, 1948 Consequences: Resignation of the co-founder, fifteen years after the opening
Après quelques jours de conclusions, Dre: After a few days of finding, Dreier writes to the Gropius that the dice is discarded: he cannot undertake another reorganization, he wants to leave; he joins the Gropius with the official sending of his resignation, then remains a time for the transition to Albers. Words: “Le dé est enfin jeté. […] J'ai dit que je voulais partir.” Atmosphere: Quiet resolution after fifteen years of struggle Issue: The co-founder leaves the work of his life
Manuscrit manuscrit non titré portant la: Manuscript untitled bearing the mention “September 11, 1948 BMC” Manuscript document kept at the Albers Foundation
Manuscrit manuscrit d'Albers daté du 11: Manuscript by Albers dated September 11, 1948: education as art means order, opposition to chaos, dirt and confusion.
Lanier écrit à Asawa pour justifier son: Lanier writes to Asawa to justify its refusal to become a partner of Tin Angel: such a project would harm its establishment as an architect. Quote: “What would have happened to Bill de Kooning if he had taken a job as a jewelry salesman” Consequences: He refuses Tolk-Watkins's partnership offer
Six extérieurs invités à discuter de leu: Six outsiders invited to discuss their role as trustees: day 1 in questions (student renewal cause, northern Caroline legal responsibilities, guarantees that internal disturbances will cease); Day 2 in suggestions: tuition increased to $1,800, loan funds instead of discounts, maximum aid capped at $900, mortgage on property, art fields, music, writing with visiting faculty, “publicité rapide et dramatique” campaign, organization of elders, concrete program and budget. They're asking for another month before committing. education $1,800; capped aid $900. Consequences: Deferred to January 1949.
Premier jour : questions sur le renouvel: Day one: questions about student body renewal, legal responsibilities in Caroline North, guarantees against new internal disturbances; Second day: budget and programmatic suggestions, then refusal to commit before audits. Words: “Des assurances peuvent-elles être données que des troubles internes ne continueront pas d'apparaître à Black Mountain ?” Atmosphere: Discretionary mistrust, audit Issue: The college must submit to the outside look it has always fled
Lettre conservée dans les archives Ruth: Letter kept in archives Ruth Asawa Lanier, Inc., cited by the source. Document dated 6 January 1949
Formulaire « Annual Report Blank of Nort: Form “Annual Report Blank of North Carolina Colleges” of 13 January 1949 to the archives of Raleigh provides the registration figures; a new student (Kelly) found Albers “très amer” facing departures: the fact that so many students leave “le bouleversait plus que les départs de la faculté”. Consequences: Albers ready to take over reorganization
Pittenger, trésorier retraité de Swarthm: Pittenger, retired treasurer of Swarthmore, friend and confidant of Frank Aydelotte (brother of Nell Rice, long-time advisor to the founders), sent by Aydelotte to investigate the school's options; it remains from 27 to 30 January but does not attend the meeting of 29. 4 days stay Consequences: Hard report on faculty
La lettre annonçant la réunion leur avai: La letter announcing the meeting had been sent to New York at the Albers merchant Sidney Janis, but had not arrived in time. Consequences: Feeling of being kept away
Les Albers reviennent de New York le 27: The Albers returned from New York on 27 January and discovered that a meeting on the fate of the college was held without them on 14 January; the invitation letter, sent to their merchant Sidney Janis, had never arrived in time Atmosphere: Feeling of conspiracy, exclusion Issue: The power of Albers collapses; his departure in May is announced
Asawa ouvre l'enveloppe : brochure aérie: Asawa opens the envelope: Sausalito's aerial brochure, “city of homes”, with the location of the Tin Angel annotated by Peggy's hand and a sarcastic “ha !” Words: The irony of Peggy versus the word “homes” Atmosphere: A mocking distance to the mass real estate dream Issue: Confrontation of Asawa, still to BMC, to post-war domesticity
Pittenger écrit à Aydelotte avec des pré: Pittenger wrote to Aydelotte with prejudices barely veiled against the Germans and against the rise of art in the college; he calls Anni “witch” (witch) and writes that Albers alone is radically different from Albers to his wife; in postscript: if Dreier leaves now, Albers will start at the end of the semester. Consequences: Alboers replied the same day (letter to Pittenger, February 1, 1949) and then to the Committee of Friends on February 3rd.
De Kooning lit un texte intitulé « A Des: De Kooning reads a text entitled “A Desperate View” during a Friday night discussion of the new Art School Subjects of the Artist. Text reproduced by Thomas B. Hess, p. 15.
Lettre signée « Kim » adressée à « Lesli: Signed letter “Kim” addressed to “Leslie” with typed “Copy for Mr. Albers” at the top of the sheet. Carbon copy, JAAF archive
Selon Fuller, seconde structure géodésiq: According to Fuller, the second 14-foot geodetic structure (approximately 4.3 m) in diameter, erected in the garden of the Pentagon building. fourteen feet in diameter; reported in a letter to Dean Wells Bennett, University of Michigan, May 14, 1949
Lanier écrit à ses parents que nulle par: Lanier writes to her parents that nowhere is the competition between architects as harsh as in California, and that the best job is required.
Lettre d'Albert Lanier à Ruth Asawa daté: Letter from Albert Lanier to Ruth Asawa dated April 20, 1949, retained at Ruth Asawa Lanier, Inc. — period of their relationship around Black Mountain College. Letter of 20 April 1949
Breton dénonce le traitement des Noirs e: Breton denounces the treatment of blacks and Indians by the US, sexual hypocrisy, the Digests, Coca-Cola, the control over Latin America and the imperialist plan over Europe. Coca-Cola and Digests explicitly appointed
Le nouveau Board of Fellows envoie une l: The new Board of Fellows sends an official letter to the “Amis du collège” announcing the new deal. Consequences: Institutionalization of the new power
Dreier confie à Duberman (1967) qu'on l': Dreier told Duberman (1967) that he was accused of trying to deliver Black Mountain to the University of Caroline in the North, simply because he had asked his president Frank Graham if he would be interested in the college in the event of bankruptcy. Consequences: Powers distrust towards Dreier
Une note de trois pages de Fuller datée: A three-page note of Fuller dated June 1, 1949 contains his remark on the “plomberie”; The sale of gravel and the Forbes case are documented by Pittenger-Trayer correspondence (25 and 30 March 1949). 3 page note Consequences: Capital income for the college
Proposition de Sawyer discutée en réunio: Sawyer's proposal discussed at a meeting on Saturday, 9 July 1949; Kahn develops “Collaborative Problem—1949: An Idea Center for Plastics” (manuscript dated “8.11”), annotated by Kahn. Bayer and Kauffer had been suggested as early as 1948. Tapuscrit annotated by Kahn, Kahn Collection, University of Pennsylvania; Albers letter to Sawyer of 23 July 1949 Consequences: Albers participates; photos of Kahn with students published in PAS, 1950 directory of the department of architecture
Lettre (timbrée 12 juillet 1949) remerci: Letter (stamped 12 July 1949) thanking for the good time, pointing out Mr. Kean's visit with Dr. Penniman who came the day before while he was working on a fresco, then complaining: the girls swear terribly, drink gin, treat the boys with dirty names; it was called “grandma” and pious; even teachers use obscene language in progress; A certain Arnold is wonderful. Fresque in progress; gin; sobriquet “grandma”; not applicable
Lettre (tampon postal du 12 juillet 1949: Letter (postal stamp of July 12, 1949) to his sister Ca and his brother-in-law Bill, printed with his original faults: Dawson is indignant that the girls drink gin and insult the boys, that he was treated with “grandma” and pinch, that even the teachers swear, and that a brilliant man uses obscene in a course. gin, tolerated beer, sobriquet “grandma”, postal stamp July 12, 1949
Photo d'Arnold Newman : Pollock, 37 ans,: Photo by Arnold Newman: 37-year-old Pollock, crossed arms in workwear splashed with paint in front of his 18-foot canvas Number 9. Title: “Est-il le plus grand peintre vivant des États-Unis ?” First recognition of the small world of downtown art by mainstream media. Bill jokes: Pollock looks like a pumpman. 18-foot canvas ( Consequences: New York School Media Consecration.
Ouverture d'une exposition de textiles d: Opening of a textile exhibition by Anni Albers announced by the New York Times; widely covered by the press (Interiors, Christian Science Monitor, New York Herald Tribune, Craft Horizons). Covers: Interiors 109 (Oct. 1949) “Power Behind the Loom”; Christian Science Monitor (19 Oct. 1949) “Anni Albers' Textiles Serve, Not Dominate, Architecture” ; Herald Tribune (25 Sept. 1949) on panels suspended as flexible partitions Consequences: Consecration of Anni Albers as textile artist in the United States
Fuller écrit à Snelson pour lui rendre c: Fuller writes to Snelson to give him credit in all his public conferences for the original demonstration of the structural advantage of discontinuous pressures and continuous tensions, and salutes him as “un vrai pionnier” we will ever know. Letter dated 22 December 1949, Fuller Papers; “Energetic Geometry” Reference Consequences: Determines that the tension/compression structure comes first from Snelson
Howe, ancien partenaire de Kahn, résiden: Howe, a former partner of Kahn, has been a resident of the American Academy in Rome since 1947, arriving at Yale on 1 January 1950 in the midst of a collaborative problem. Consequences: Duo Howe–Albers at the head of art school.
Conférence donnée dans le cadre du progr: Lecture given as part of the gallery programme; Howe probably present, freshly arrived.
Carte tapée à la machine de biais pour f: Card typed with bias machine to form a diamond, signed “love kk”, with two short poems (“These Days” and “The Day's Orders, Boys”) and a comment on Saroyan. “11 pm Jan 29 (?) 1950” stamp; signature in tiny “yrs, kk” with k Greek
Albers continue de demander « les 20 % a: Albers continues to claim “les 20 % autres” of what it calls its pension fund; the question remains alive for a long time. Council Minutes of February 22, 1950 (?) Consequences: Persistent Albers resentment towards college
Un « comité d'établissement des faits »: A “comité d'établissement des faits” (Goldowski, Hetherington and two students, Vera Williams and Andy Oates) writes a five-page report summarizing both positions. 5 Page Report Consequences: Formalization of both camps
Olson, apres un match Browns de St. Loui: Olson, after a Browns game of St. Louis–Senators of Washington (winner 5-4 in 12 rounds), sends Dawson an annotation and drawing score card, posted by Washington on June 3, 1950. cardboard folded in half; Name of Dawson writes first family name (game on Ostrowski, voltigeur des Senators); curved ink lines to “YR BOYS” and “DID ALL RIGHT!”; semi-circle draws with tiny words on Ostrowski and Michaels, second goal Consequences: Dawson reads a visual message announcing The Rose of the World
Mémorandum de Howe : les conditions de t: Howe's memorandum: working conditions can be described as intolerable — complaint similar to that of Albers
Albers écrit : « Une de mes conditions e: Albers writes: “Une de mes conditions est de pouvoir éviter l'essentiel de l'administration”
Albers conserve dans sa collection de co: Albers keeps in its press clipping collection a photograph of the New York Herald Tribune showing about 90 sailboats seen from the sky, massed in the Long Island Sound for the departure of the Larchmont Race Week; She looks like her “schools of fish” exercise. About 90 sailboats; newspaper of 16 July 1950. Consequences: Illustrating his passion for “relatedness”, harmoniously linked forms.
Albers écrit au collège une lettre d'une: Albers wrote to the college a single sentence, furious, demanding that neither he nor his wife be mentioned in the college's publications that retained his property and did not respond to his letters. Letter of one sentence; further letter from Albers to the Council of January 17, 1952 Consequences: Final symbolic termination between Albers and BMC
Albers, excédé par le silence du collège: Albers, overridden by the college's silence on his property, writes a single sentence demanding that he and Anni no longer be mentioned in the college's publications Words: “Nous, ma femme et moi, ne souhaitons pas être mentionnés dans les publications du collège qui retient ma propriété et ne répond pas à mes lettres” Atmosphere: Final Coldness Issue: Out of the artistic founder with the institution
Malrey a rôti d'avance un dindon énorme: Malrey roasted a huge turkey in advance (she and Cornelia were off), helped by Mary Fiore and several students and professors; Rumaker puts white sheets of North Lodge linen in tablecloths, finds short candles for each table (we never used tablecloths or candles, even for Saturday evening dressed chicken dinners); someone picked laurel, holly, pine branches and cones for the chimney and tables; T. J., the new man to everything, brings the biggest Christmas büche ever seen, lit at dawn, burning ingot red throughout the meal; wine and all the accompaniments; Merrill deigns to come, pleasant after a few glasses, then helps Rumaker dive to climb up more quickly white sheets, shorted candles, laurel/houx/pin/cones, büche filling the mouth of the large chimney in field stone, huge turkey, wine Consequences: Rumaker knows that that day that BMC is now his home; come down in a hurry with Merrill at dusk cold for love
Rumaker installe draps blancs et chandel: Rumaker installs white sheets and candles on tables; T. J. drags the biggest büche ever seen, lit with the aune, burning red ingot all the meal; turkey, wine, greenery on the mante ; Merrill, after a few glasses, becomes pleasant; Then help Rumaker dive to climb faster; both rush up in cold twilight, smoking breaths, towards the hut and duvet Atmosphere: Light of candles and büche, family warmth recovered, worries of the future of the college forgotten one day Issue: Rumaker recognizes BMC as his home; idyll at its summit — “jamais je n'ai été si heureux”
Life publie la photo des quatorze hommes: Life published the photo of the fourteen men and the only woman (Hedda Tern, placed to dominate the group), nicknamed “Irascibles Eighteen” by the Herald Tribune of 23 May 1950, dressed respectably, “comme des banquiers”, at the request of Newman. 14 men, 1 woman; Three colleagues absent from the photo shoot.
Willem de Kooning écrit le texte « What: Willem of Kooning writes the text “What Abstract Art Means to Me” for a symposium at MoMA, then published in the Museum Bulletin. Text published in The Bulletin of The Museum of Modern Art, pp. 4-5
À l'occasion de l'exposition Abstract Pa: On the occasion of the exhibition Abstract Painting and Sculpture in America (January 1951, with Excavation), by Kooning wrote “What Abstract Art Means to Me” for the symposium and had his text read by Andrew Carnduff Ritchie, then director of MoMA's department of painting and sculpture: some painters, including him, found that painting — all kinds, all styles of painting — to be painting in fact, is a way of living today, a lifestyle. Text published in MoMA Bulletin 18 (Spring 1951).
Trop excité pour respecter les frontière: Too excited to respect the boundaries of words, Olson opens its March 17 letter by “christamiexcited”; later, the “f” key on his machine breaks and unleashes a line of swears that ironically culminates in “fuck it”. Words: “christamiexcited”; “fuck it” Atmosphere: Epistolar excitation, writing fever in a foreign climate Issue: Writing as a body flow, the machine itself participating
Les Blueprints du couple paraissent dans: The couple's Blueprints appear in a three-page article (“Speaking of Pictures”) by Life (p. 22-24); They then contact their friends Liberman and Brodovich to find work thanks to this sudden notoriety. “Beaucoup de promesses alléchantes, aucun travail”
Les « Blueprints » du couple sont présen: The couple's “Blueprints” are presented in a three-page Life article. pp. 22-24 of the magazine Consequences: rapid notoriety but no job obtained
Dawson et quatre camarades (Carl, Tim, W: Dawson and four comrades (Carl, Tim, Webber, Joel) saw the Brooklyn Dodgers beat 9-8 the Asheville Tourists (class B): Campanella (receiver) hit two circuits, Robinson (second goal) an inner circuit; Duke Snider runs behind a bullet in the center and just ahead of six kids invading the field. The children cheer the blacks, most adults support the local team; a spectator makes racist comments and Joel, Tim and Webber change places. The blacks, deprived of seats, stand by thousands along the left field line; a great black lady runs through each circuit of Campanella and, in the third, rips off her hat by screaming, triggering the hilarity of the stands. score 9-8; Asheville 3 runs in 1st, 4 in 3rd, 1 in 6th; Brooklyn 3 in 4th, 3 in 5th, 3 in 7th; 4 hours match; stadium of about 1500 seats, at least 5000 spectators, about one sixth of blacks; return just in time for dinner
Manche par manche, Brooklyn renverse Ash: Sleeve per sleeve, Brooklyn overturns Asheville and wins 9-8; at each circuit of Campanella a great black lady ran to photograph him; in the second, she rips off her hat and turns around screaming — the whole stadium dies of laughter; Snider fights a ball from the center field to six kids; Joel, Tim and Webber leave a racist neighbor to join Carl and Dawson; Back just in time for dinner. Atmosphere: exhausted crowd, stirring, hilarious; Four hours of sunshine Issue: segregation cracked by sport and laughter
La rubrique « Speaking of Pictures » de: La section “Speaking of Pictures” of Life publishes an article with photographs of the blueprint experiences of Rauschenberg and Susan Weil. section “Speaking of Pictures”, Life, 19 April 1951 Consequences: MoMA exhibition in the same year
Un article avec photographies de leurs e: An article with photographs of their blueprint experiences appears in Life's “Speaking of Pictures” section. Life, 19 April 1951, heading “Speaking of Pictures”
Dans sa lettre de démission, Leser écrit: In his resignation letter, Leser wrote that he found BMC “la véritable constitution et pratique démocratiques” that he was looking for when he left Olivet; his departure is purely personal; “je suis amoureux de [Black Mountain] et je la sens telle qu'elle doit être”. Letter to Council of April 24, 1951 Consequences: Departure of a beloved teacher
En séance réservée aux membres, Elaine d: In a member-only session, Elaine says it believes more in van Gogh: a distorted look or figure is an irrational whim; Bill disapproves of “de l'intérieur” (German Expressionists) distortion as “de l'extérieur” (Subtle, Bacon); Elaine recalls the word of Vlaminck: a phone wire carrying emotion is painted with a undulating trait 17 male artists around it Consequences: illustration of the aplomb of Elaine, the only woman 33 years old facing men
Time magazine publie un article surnomma: Time magazine publishes an article nicknamed Kooning “Willem the Walloper”, p. 63.
Peu après son arrivée, Shahn livre dans: Shortly after his arrival, Shahn delivered a captivating lecture in the refectory where he imagined the answers of a psychologist, a physicist, an art critic, etc., to the same picture, to show the contingence of the aspects of realism, which he defined as “une recherche sincère de la vérité dans le cadre de ses propres valeurs”. transcription held at Black Mountain College Project Papers, Western Regional Archives, Asheville
Devant la communauté réunie pour manger,: In front of the community gathered to eat, Shahn improvises a series of fictional looks on a picture — psychologist, physicist, critic — and defines realism as a sincere search for truth within the framework of its own values. Words: Realism like “an earnest search for truth within the framework of one's own values” Atmosphere: captivating conference, ordinary dining room transformed into an amphitheater Issue: A social realistic in the middle of the abstracts of summer 1951 (Motherwell)
Inspiré par l'échange de glyphes, Olson: Inspired by the exchange of glyphs, Olson asked his friend W. H. Ferry for funds for the college, pleading for the importance of the joint work of artists of different disciplines in America of 1951. Consequences: attempt to fund the college
Lettre d'Imogen Cunningham au couple, tr: Letter from Imogen Cunningham to the couple, trace of their friendship.
Lors de la réunion de faculté du 2 novem: At the faculty meeting on November 2, 1951, Olson stated that it believed in “la liberté absolue de l'étudiant, la liberté même de se concentrer sur une seule matière”. Minutes of the October-November 1951 meetings Consequences: Educational debate of the new Black Mountain
En réunion de faculté, Huss commente ave: At the faculty meeting, Huss comments in a good mood that Olson would make a bad member of the Community Council: its most valuable contribution is to raise things to a certain level of energy; “Olson n'était pas fou comme administrateur” (not so hot). Minutes of 9 November 1951; pleasant tone by context Consequences: Debate on the role of Olson in governance
Litz danse The Glyph à New York le 23 dé: Litz dances The Glyph at New York on December 23, 1951.
Il neige depuis deux heures, température: It's been snowing for two hours, temperature falling. Olson wants to drain the radiator valve from his car and look for a flashlight. In the refectory, Twombly plays the organ with three students (guitar, drums, piano) of Morton Feldman's music; Twombly tells him a lamp is in the car of Rauschenberg. Rauschenberg, who played the canasta at the farm, exits barefoot from the refectory and enters the ice lake; Twombly follows it until half-body six meters from the edge and then turns back; Rauschenberg turns around, Twombly guides ("This way Bob"), Olson brings blankets and the door half to the kitchen of the refectory, warms it near the snow fire for two hours, black night, Twombly 20 feet from the shore (up to the hips), Rauschenberg towards the middle of the lake, smaller and hiccups of the voice, two flashlights, blankets, electric stove, eyes without focus, Olson smells cold in his ankles by lying down Consequences: Olson writes the next day to Robert Creeley; four men sitting in the kitchen ignore the scene, one smiling with satisfaction; suicide attempt or attention cry, unsettled
Neige et chute de température ; Olson de: Snow and temperature drop; Olson goes down to the refectory looking for a flashlight to drain its radiator; Twombly and three students beat Feldman's music (organ, guitar, drums, piano); "Dommage que tu n'aies pas été là plus tôt, on la déchirait vraiment, maintenant ça s'aplatit"; the lamp is in the Rauschenberg car; Rauschenberg, hovered by the canasta, comes barefoot, "soufflé par la pression" from the music; "Bob, mets tes chaussures"; Olson, exhausted, wants to return to Constance and Kate; Cree in the dark: "Olson, la lampe, vite !"; it runs, passes the lamp to Cernovich: a beam discovers a head in the water; Twombly at six meters, to the hips, breath cut; Rauschenberg further towards the middle, moaning and voices that cut; Olson wraps his coat, thinks of diving, runs for the raft; Twombly turns back, defeated by the cold; Rauschenberg turns back; Twombly returns to him by cooing "Par ici Bob, par ici"; blankets, second lamp, outlet of water; Olson carries it half to the kitchen, wet against it; four men at the kitchen table ignore the scene, one smiling with passive pleasure; Twombly alone keeps its dignity, vaulted silently on an electric stove; Olson sleeps with cold ankles, falls asleep as if he had been in the lake Words: Twombly : we were really tearing it / Bob put on your shoes / This way Bob, over here ; cry: Olson, the lamp, fast! Olson to Creeley: he said that he could not go further, that he did not resume his breath Atmosphere: black night, snow, ice water, trembling lamp, adrenaline, consternation, repulsion of Olson for the body wet against him Issue: attempted suicide or shout of attention of a man torn between his wife and the man he loves, before the eyes of the one who despises and saves him
